interfaces.name: eye_ring_seat
interfaces.what: the front face, plane y -55.5000 (the mesh's own y minimum), with a Ø14.5000 x 1.3000 aperture on the optical axis at (0.0000, -54.8500, 20.0000), axis y, residual 0.0000 mm at 355.0 deg. part:microduck-eye-ring butts here: its Ø30.0000 x 7.5000 outer ring spans y -63.0000..-55.5000 in this SAME frame (both meshes carry the identical MJCF placement, body jaw_soft at [25.9, -0.0914, 231.1146]), so the ring's Ø30.0000 SHOULDER and this front face meet at y -55.5000 EXACTLY, and its Ø14.4000 bore is coaxial with this Ø14.5000 aperture. AND THE RING DOES NOT STOP THERE: part:microduck-eye-ring's own folder measures a Ø19.0000 x 1.5000 rear SPIGOT continuing from y -55.5000 to the ring mesh's y maximum -54.0000, which enters this panel. The two folders now say the same thing; lane T's first reading of this row stopped at the Ø30 shoulder and was incomplete, and lane A's spigot measurement (2026-09-03) completes it. THE DECIMATED MESH OF THIS PART REGISTERS NO Ø19 RECESS on that axis — only the Ø14.5000 aperture — so where the spigot lands is CANNOT DETERMINE from geometry. `accepts` is EMPTY on purpose: the joint between them is a butt face with no measured fastener, groove or barb on either mesh, and no connection folder on this shelf describes it. Naming one would dangle; inventing one would be worse.
interfaces.source: MEASURED off Pollen's face_part.stl by cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders and the mesh bbox, frozen 2026-09-02 by tools/measure_mesh_features.py into out/laneT/features/face_part.json (lane T); the MJCF places this mesh in body 'jaw_soft' at world [25.9, -0.0914, 231.1146] mm, quat (wxyz) [0.707107, 0.0, 0.0, 0.707107] (ce-assemblies/microduck/current/placements.json); the Ø19.0000 x 1.5000 rear spigot is lane A's measurement on the same mesh, recorded in part:microduck-eye-ring cad/interfaces.json 'face_seat' (2026-09-03)

interfaces.name: camera_mount
interfaces.what: 4 x Ø1.6000 x 4.2500 thread-forming pilots at (x, z) = (+-6.7500, 9.5000) and (+-6.7500, 30.5000) — a 13.5000 x 21.0000 mm rectangle on a Ø24.9650 circle — each on a Ø4.5000 x 6.7000 boss (centres y -50.8500) and each relieved by a Ø2.2000 x 0.7500 counterbore at y -47.3750. Axis y. Ø1.6 is cecad.fasteners' M2 tap drill, so these are self-tapping M2 into printed bosses. Residual 0.0000 mm at 355.0 deg on all twelve features.

interfaces.name: front_pair
interfaces.what: 2 x Ø2.0500 x 4.0000 at (x, y, z) = (32.4000, -53.2000, 20.0000) and (12.6000, -53.2000, 20.0000), axis +y, 19.8000 mm apart, on the front face beside the eye aperture. Frame origin is their midpoint. WHAT THEY FASTEN IS CANNOT DETERMINE: they are the only asymmetric pattern on this part (both on the +x side of the optical axis), no mesh in any of Pollen's four MJCF files carries a matching pair, and no document in this repo names them. What settles it: a photograph of the face plate's front with the bezel off, or the head assembly from Pollen.

source.declared_shelf_frame: Pollen's mesh frame for face_part.stl: bbox x -43.8253..43.8253, y -55.5000..-43.0000, z -0.8000..43.8265 (87.6507 x 12.5000 x 44.6265 mm); the optical axis is the y-line through (x 0.0000, z 20.0000) and the front face is the plane y -55.5000.
